analysis: The recency-weighted, per-history loss achieved validation macro HR@10 of 0.4963, improving by 0.0051 over the reported prior sampled-softmax result of 0.4912, but remaining 0.0087 below the reported baseline of 0.505. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.575, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.505, Electronics 0.390, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.515. Electronics improved from the reported prior 0.375 but remained below its reported baseline of 0.420. The macro improvement meets the lower end of the hypothesized gain; this single experiment does not establish causality or separate recency weighting from history balancing. The host reported success and 436.69 allocated GPU-seconds. No test results were available.
code_summary: Trains one independent SASRec model per category from scratch with seed 42 and loads one selected checkpoint per category at inference. Architecture remains a 96-dimensional, two-block, two-head causal Transformer with pre-layer normalization, GELU feed-forward layers, dropout 0.2, learned positional embeddings, maximum history length 64, normalized item/features, learned temperature, and item biases. Training retains prefix augmentation, AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, 256 sampled negatives, training-history exclusion masks, and at most 24 randomly selected transitions per history. The changed reduction applies unreduced cross-entropy weighted by 2^(-d/8), where d measures distance from the final target in the supplied window; float32 scatter-add normalizes within each history before averaging valid histories equally. Prepared splits, four-category routing, validation setup, predictor architecture, and single-checkpoint inference are retained; no ensembles or separately fitted auxiliary scores are used.
